title: U.S. House · Colorado's 1st District

context.text: This is an open seat: Melat Kiros defeated incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette and Wanda James 53.2%-39.8%-7.0% in the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary, so DeGette will not appear on the November ballot. Christy Peterson advanced unopposed from the Republican primary.

candidates.name: Melat Kiros
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary, defeating incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette

summary.text: Melat Kiros is the Democratic nominee for Colorado's 1st District, a 29-year-old former attorney and graduate student who immigrated from Ethiopia as a child. A first-time candidate, she defeated 15-term incumbent Rep. Diana DeGette in the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary. She identifies as a democratic socialist and describes her priorities as health care, housing, and campaign-finance and anti-corruption reform.

background.text: Immigrated to Denver from Tigray, Ethiopia, with her family in 1998, according to her Ballotpedia survey; Reuters reports she moved to the U.S. as a baby. She describes herself as the daughter of Ethiopian immigrants and the first lawyer in her family.
Earned bachelor's degrees in Political Science and Economics from Washington College (2018) and a law degree from the University of Notre Dame (2022).

Worked as a lawyer; Reuters reports she was fired from her job after refusing to remove a post criticizing law firms' stance on Israel and Palestine. She says she was fired from the firm Sidley Austin for defending students' right to protest the war in Gaza.

Worked as a barista; in her 2026 Colorado Politics questionnaire she describes herself as a renter with student debt who was, until recently, a tipped-wage barista at Whittier Cafe, and Colorado Politics describes her as a graduate student.
Entered the race as a first-time candidate and won the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary over Rep. Diana DeGette, who had held the seat since 1997, and University of Colorado Regent Wanda James.
Her Ballotpedia survey and campaign materials say she is running to reduce the influence of money in politics; she says she does not accept corporate PAC money.

priorities.text: Campaign finance and lobbying reform, plus congressional term limits, to reduce the influence of money in politics.
Expanding voting rights and consolidating elections into a single day with a shorter election cycle.
Codifying access to housing, health care, nutritious food and public education as basic needs for every American.

positions.summary: Campaign website says she will always stand for Medicare for All and describes health care access as directly linked to life expectancy and economic outcomes.
Says she will always stand for universal childcare as part of putting working families first.
Campaign website calls for an arms embargo, saying U.S. tax dollars have funded what she describes as a genocide in Palestine.

summary.text: Christy Peterson is the Republican nominee for Colorado's 1st District. She works as an office manager and bookkeeper at a construction company in the Denver Tech Center and is pursuing a doctorate in natural and functional medicine. She says she is running on public safety, lower taxes and limited government.

background.text: According to her campaign biography as reported by the Denver Gazette, she was born and raised in Colorado; her Ballotpedia survey says she is from the Lakewood/Littleton area and she now lives in south Denver.
Graduated from Chatfield Senior High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from San Diego State University in 2006.
Works as an office manager and bookkeeper for a small construction contractor, according to the Denver Gazette; describes herself as a designer and accountant working in construction.
States she is working on a PhD in natural and functional medicine.

In her Ballotpedia survey she says she decided to become a leader in the Republican Party after events in 2020 and 2025. She was the only Republican to run for the district's nomination and was unopposed.

priorities.text: Public safety: says reducing crime and 'soft on crime' policies in Denver is her top priority, arguing this would let businesses and visitors return to the city.
Reducing government waste, fraud and abuse, and creating incentives for business growth and job creation.

positions.summary: Lists the Save America Act among the measures she supports in her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.
positions.quote: Yes to election integrity, the Save America Act, paper ballots, same day voting & hand count.

candidates.name: Chad Humphrey

summary.text: Chad Humphrey is the Libertarian Party candidate for Colorado's 1st District. According to his Ballotpedia survey, he is a retired Marine Corps officer with a combat tour who now works as a technology entrepreneur. His stated campaign messages are to restore the Constitution, end the Federal Reserve and the IRS, and stop endless wars.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Marine Corps Reserve from 1993 to 2013; his survey describes him as a retired Marine Corps officer who completed a combat tour.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Occidental College and an MBA from Pepperdine University.
Works as a technology entrepreneur / technology professional.
Nominated as the Libertarian Party candidate for Colorado's 1st District in the November 3, 2026 general election; Ballotpedia lists no prior elected offices.

priorities.text: Lists his three key campaign messages as restoring the Constitution, ending the Federal Reserve and the IRS, and stopping what he calls endless wars.
Says he is personally passionate about free markets.

candidates.researchNotes: Completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, which did not directly address any of the guide's tracked issue statements; no separate campaign website was found.

candidates.name: Shimon Blau

summary.text: Shimon Blau is an unaffiliated candidate for Colorado's 1st District, a 50-year-old Denver-born physician and small-business owner. He launched his campaign and petitioned onto the ballot within days of the June 2026 Democratic primary. His campaign lists affordability, health care reform and economic growth as priorities and says he rejects PAC contributions.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he was born and raised in Denver's Sloan's Lake neighborhood, the son of immigrants George and Hermine; his father was a Holocaust survivor from Poland who served in the U.S. Army during the Korean War and earned an engineering degree from Columbia University, and his mother was from France.
Left Denver at age 13 to pursue his education; medical school, residency and specialized training took him across the country, per his campaign website.
Is a board-certified physician specializing in interventional spine and pain management; returned to Denver in 2013 to complete his fellowship and build his medical practice.
Describes himself in a Colorado Politics questionnaire as a physician with more than 20 years of experience and a small business owner.
Age 50 per Colorado Politics. Entered the race as an unaffiliated candidate within days of Melat Kiros's primary win and qualified for the ballot by petition.
His campaign website says he and his wife live in Denver.

priorities.text: Says he is running as an independent who rejects contributions from PACs and special-interest groups, saying he answers only to the people of the district.

Says he would caucus with Democrats and support Rep. Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker as a check on the Trump administration, while remaining willing to oppose Democratic-backed policies he disagrees with.
Wants to strengthen Denver's local economy by supporting small businesses, encouraging investment, and improving public safety.

positions.summary: In a Colorado Politics voter guide he says criminal aliens who threaten public safety should be deported, and also calls for fast-tracking legal status for long-term residents and for training and accountability for immigration agents.
positions.quote: Criminal aliens who threaten public safety should be deported, and our streets must be safer. At the same time, we should fast-track legal status for long-term, contributing members of our communities who have built their lives here.

candidates.researchNotes: No Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response found; background and positions are drawn from his campaign website (blauforcongress.com), which does not have a dedicated issues page but discusses his priorities on the home page.

statements.quote: I support a woman's right to make her own healthcare decisions
statements.context: On his campaign website; the page does not use the word abortion

candidates.name: Critter Milton

summary.text: Critter Milton is the Unity Party candidate for Colorado's 1st Congressional District, a former financial advisor who lives in Alma, Colorado.

background.text: Earned a degree from the University of Denver in 2006 and attended the College for Financial Planning for graduate study.
In his 2020 and 2022 Ballotpedia surveys he says he spent over a decade as a financial advisor and has done extensive backcountry exploration and volunteer work.
Lives in Alma, Colorado, according to his 2022 Ballotpedia survey.
Member of the organizing committee of Multiple Summits for Multiple Sclerosis.

Ran as the Unity Party candidate for Colorado's 3rd District in 2020, Colorado's 7th District in 2022, and this seat in 2024; Ballotpedia also lists him among withdrawn candidates for the 2020 Democratic U.S. Senate primary.

priorities.text: In his most recent completed Ballotpedia survey (2022), listed his three key campaign messages simply as 'Unity, Unity, Unity.'
In an earlier (2020) survey, said his priorities included free universal education using technology, action on climate change, and ending prohibition by legalizing currently banned substances.

candidates.researchNotes: Milton has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; his most recent completed survey was in 2022 (for a different U.S. House race), so priorities above are dated and not necessarily current for this 2026 campaign. No campaign website with current issue positions was found.

researchNotes: Federal key votes and FEC finance totals are added separately by script (not applicable to non-incumbents in this open-seat race). Chad Humphrey completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; Shimon Blau has an active campaign website with priorities and one clear issue position; Critter Milton's Ballotpedia biography and most recent completed survey (2022, for a different race) provide some background, though he has not completed a 2026 survey. Write-in candidates from the primary (StClair, Wren, Replin) are omitted as not having active general-election campaigns. Biography gaps: Christy Peterson's campaign did not respond to press requests and has a minimal website; Chad Humphrey and Critter Milton have only Ballotpedia survey-based biographical information.
